analysis.investment_thesis: Unisem Agritech fails the Magic Formula on both dimensions: ROE of just 0.57% signals very weak returns on capital, and a P/E of 15.9 implies an earnings yield of only ~6.3% — neither cheap nor good. Without meaningful EBIT productivity, systematic buying criteria cannot be satisfied.
key_strengths: High promoter holding of 70.88% shows skin in the game
Operates in a structurally growing Indian seeds/agri-inputs niche
Some institutional interest (FII 5.59% + DII 8.17%) unusual for a 68 Cr microcap
key_risks: ROE of 0.57% indicates near-zero return on capital — fails ROIC test decisively
Earnings yield ~6.3% at 15.9x P/E is below the 12%+ Magic Formula threshold
Microcap scale (68 Cr) + working-capital-heavy seeds business raises capital intensity concerns
red_flags: ROE of 0.57% is effectively break-even profitability
Valuation multiple unjustified by return profile
Too small and young (founded 2016) to demonstrate sustained ROIC track record
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula demands cheapness AND quality simultaneously. On quality, ROE of 0.57% is catastrophic — the business is barely earning anything on shareholder capital, which almost certainly translates to a single-digit ROIC far below my 20%+ threshold. On cheapness, a 15.9x P/E yields roughly 6.3% earnings yield, well under the 12% bar I look for. A company this marginal would need to trade at sub-5x earnings to be interesting, and it doesn't.

Seeds businesses can be attractive when they build IP and pricing power (think Kaveri Seeds in its prime), but Unisem shows none of that economics yet — it's a 10-year-old microcap with razor-thin returns. High promoter holding is a positive governance signal but cannot compensate for capital inefficiency. Systematic screens would rank this in the bottom decile on combined yield + ROIC; there is no basis to buy.
